setting: Colonists arrive at a world strung with 'alien' ruins that fit human hands too well. The makers did not fall — they erased themselves on purpose, scattered, and buried something. As the colonists recover self-referential relics (memory-cores, sealed bio-vaults, redacted star-charts, defaced monuments, encrypted wills), each handling bleeds inherited ancestral memory, and the finds accumulate toward a fixed moral reckoning: the colonists ARE the makers' descendants, and the makers chose to bury a specific, morally heavy secret. Resources are incidental to the reckoning.

civs.name: the-erased
civs.trait: the ancestral makers who deliberately deleted their own record and scattered, leaving only traces; absent-by-choice, not dead

civs.name: the-redactors
civs.trait: the maker-caste that performed the great forgetting — sealed the vaults, defaced the monuments, edited the charts; their fingerprints are on every deletion

civs.name: the-refusers
civs.trait: the maker-minority who fought the erasure and hid counter-records so a descendant could one day reassemble the truth; gone with the rest
